verses: Alas for me, still but a child! For all too soon I know The cares of the unsettled state. Too heavy will they grow. I shrink in sorrow from the task; But, O my mighty sire, To filial virtue, all thy life, Thou ever didst aspire. My great grandsire, though now enshrined, To thee still living proved, As if in courtyard and in hall His royal person moved, And I, the little child, will be As reverent night and day. To you, great kings, such homage I Now on your throne will pay.
